documents.title: Guidelines for Teaching and Learning with AI (PDF)
documents.summary: Provost-level guidelines from the AI Implementation Workgroup that encourage faculty to explore AI, leave the extent of use to each instructor, and ask for a syllabus AI statement. Three sample statements (permissive, hybrid, restrictive) are supplied, and misconduct follows the existing honor code.
documents.stance_why: The guidelines state "Faculty have the autonomy to decide the extent to which they incorporate AI tools in their courses" and supply three sample policies (permissive, hybrid, restrictive) for instructors to adopt; the document itself sets no single student rule, so it delegates with tiers.

units.why: "Faculty are encouraged to explore and integrate AI tools" is a guiding principle recommending AI use by instructors; P02 (encourage by default) fits because the stance is welcoming, though it addresses faculty teaching use rather than student work.
units.anchor: Faculty are encouraged to explore and integrate AI tools to enhance teaching and learning experiences.
units.fit_note: Addresses faculty exploring AI in teaching, not a rule for student assignments.

units.why: "AI use should align with ethical standards, respect data privacy, and comply with relevant regulations (FERPA, HIPAA, etc.)" is a principle requiring lawful and ethical use; I chose P77 (comply with law) over P50 because the main demand is regulatory compliance.
units.anchor: AI use should align with ethical standards, respect data privacy, and comply with relevant regulations

units.why: "Transparency in AI applications is essential" states a general principle of the framework, so P56 (institution-wide principles) is the fit.
units.anchor: Transparency in AI applications is essential.

units.why: "Faculty have the autonomy to decide the extent to which they incorporate AI tools in their courses" hands the decision to each instructor, which is P04.
units.anchor: Faculty have the autonomy to decide the extent to which they incorporate AI tools in

units.why: "Those who choose not to use AI will not be required to follow these guidelines" sets the scope of the guidelines (opt-out for faculty who do not use AI), so P61 (policy scope).
units.anchor: Those who choose not to use AI will not be required to follow these guidelines.

units.why: "Comprehensive training programs and resources will continue to be provided" for faculty and students commits the university to AI training; P70 fits because students are named alongside faculty.
units.anchor: Comprehensive training programs and resources will continue to be provided

units.why: "Faculty are encouraged to attend these sessions" recommends that instructors attend DTT AI training, which is faculty-only support (P63) rather than student training.
units.anchor: Faculty are encouraged to attend these sessions.

units.why: "Feedback on AI tools, trainings, and resources will be used to continuously improve AI initiatives" promises revision based on feedback, matching P54.
units.anchor: Feedback on AI tools, trainings, and resources will be used to continuously improve AI initiatives

units.why: "Faculty should familiarize themselves with the capabilities and limitations of AI tools" asks instructors to learn AI before deciding policy, which is P63.
units.anchor: Faculty should familiarize themselves with the capabilities and limitations of AI tools.

units.why: "AI tools should be used to augment, not replace, human interaction and judgment" keeps humans as the decision-maker; P32 is nearest, though it is a general principle not limited to students.
units.anchor: AI tools should be used to augment, not replace, human interaction and judgment.
units.fit_note: General principle of human judgment for all users, not specifically students as problem-solvers.

units.why: "Faculty should include a clear AI policy in their course syllabi" requires a syllabus AI statement, which is P09.
units.anchor: Faculty should include a clear AI policy in their course syllabi

units.why: "Sample policy statements for permissive, hybrid, and restrictive use" offers three named levels of AI use, so the document provides tiers (P05).
units.anchor: Sample policy statements for permissive, hybrid, and restrictive use are provided below.

units.why: "Redesign assignments to leverage AI tools where appropriate" asks instructors to restructure assignments around AI, which is P35.
units.anchor: Redesign assignments to leverage AI tools where appropriate

units.why: "design assignments to promote original student work" asks instructors to anticipate misuse in assignment design, which is P35.
units.anchor: design assignments to promote original student work

units.why: "Clearly communicate expectations regarding the use of AI tools and the consequences of misuse" tells instructors to state expectations to students, closest to P09 (state expectations), though it also covers consequences.
units.anchor: Clearly communicate expectations regarding the use of AI tools and the consequences of misuse.
units.fit_note: Also requires communicating consequences of misuse, not only expectations.

units.why: "Academic integrity misconduct will follow existing honor code and student conduct standards" routes AI misconduct to existing processes: P36.
units.anchor: Academic integrity misconduct will follow existing honor code and student conduct standards.

units.why: "Faculty will be provided with relevant tools and trainings to detect and address potential academic misconduct related to AI" promises detection tools, nearest P40, though it is a promise of tools rather than a rule on evidence.

units.fit_note: Promises detection tools and training in future; no rule on how they are used.

units.why: "Ensure AI use complies with copyright, intellectual property, and privacy laws" requires compliance with law; P77 over P52 because the rule is general legal compliance.
units.anchor: Ensure AI use complies with copyright, intellectual property, and privacy laws.

units.why: "Protect sensitive data and comply with FERPA and HIPAA regulations" directs data protection when using AI in teaching: P50.
units.anchor: Protect sensitive data and comply with FERPA and HIPAA regulations

units.why: "Use AI tools in a manner that supports diversity, inclusion, and accessibility" is an equity expectation; P51 is nearest though it does not mention cost or alternatives.
units.anchor: Use AI tools in a manner that supports diversity, inclusion, and accessibility.

units.anchor: We expect that all the work students submit for this course will be their own.

documents.title: BOV Policy 1220: Standards for the Safe Use of Artificial Intelligence
documents.summary: A Board of Visitors policy on responsible, ethical AI across research, teaching and administration, binding all employees. It sets principles (ethics, innovation, privacy, equity), requires vendor and approval review and data protection, and provides for training and annual review; it does not set classroom rules for student AI use.
documents.stance_why: The board policy commits to "Encourage innovation and experimentation in AI integration" while setting conditions on ethics, privacy, vendor approval and compliance, so AI use is allowed with conditions (permit); it sets no student-level rule.

units.why: Option C allows students to "generate content for your assignments, provided that the content is accurate, unbiased, and appropriate": P16 (conditional AI-generated output).
units.anchor: provided that the content is accurate, unbiased, and appropriate for the assignment
units.fit_note: Applies to all generated content, not specifically code, and the condition is accuracy and appropriateness.

units.why: "(1) specify which AI tool you used" in Option C requires naming the tool: P25.
units.anchor: you must (1) specify which AI tool you used

units.why: "use quotation marks or a different font color to distinguish AI-generated content" marks AI content at the place it appears: P27.
units.anchor: use quotation marks or a different font color to distinguish AI-generated content

units.why: The citation guidance asks "What prompt did you use to generate the content?" and also tool, content used, how it was used and date: P25.
units.anchor: What prompt did you use to generate the content?
units.policy: Students who acknowledge AI use state the tool, the prompt, the content used, how the results were used, and the date.

units.why: "Keep drafts of your work to show how AI was used to complete the assignment" asks students to keep drafts as evidence: P26.
units.anchor: Keep drafts of your work to show how AI was used to complete the assignment.

units.why: "AI-generated content may not always be accurate or unbiased" warns students to check output: P31.
units.anchor: AI-generated content may not always be accurate or unbiased.

units.why: "Paid subscriptions provide access to more powerful models" names an equity problem from paid tiers: P51.
units.anchor: Paid subscriptions provide access to more powerful models with advanced features.

units.why: "AIGCTs collect user data, so it is important not to share any personal information" tells students to protect personal data: P50.
units.anchor: AIGCTs collect user data, so it is important not to share any personal information.

units.why: "Consider the potential for misuse of AI-generated content, such as creating misleading information or deepfakes" asks instructors to address deceptive AI use: P74 fits partly.
units.anchor: Consider the potential for misuse of AI-generated content, such as creating misleading information or deepfakes
units.fit_note: Asks instructors to consider and prevent misuse; no conduct ban for students.

units.why: "Emphasize transparency in the use of AI tools" so content is "properly attributed" asks instructors to stress attribution: P24 fits partly.

units.fit_note: Addressed to instructors to emphasize attribution, not a student disclosure duty.

units.why: "Discuss the potential impact of AI-generated content on society, such as the potential for job displacement or the spread of misinformation" names societal harms: P53.

units.why: "Recognize that AICGTs require human oversight to ensure accuracy and appropriateness of content" says output needs human checking: P31.

units.why: "Encourage critical thinking and skepticism in the use of AICGTs" asks instructors to promote skeptical use: P31 fits partly.
units.anchor: Encourage critical thinking and skepticism in the use of AICGTs
units.fit_note: Frames verification as a teaching aim rather than a student duty.

units.why: "Learn about the subtle clues that can indicate AI-generated content, such as unusual phrasing or lack of context" suggests spotting AI by textual clues; P40 fits partly (it names process evidence and tools, not stylistic clues).
units.anchor: Learn about the subtle clues that can indicate AI-generated content, such as unusual phrasing or
units.fit_note: Stylistic clues like unusual phrasing, not software or process evidence.

units.why: "Become familiar with available tools that can help detect AI-generated text" asks instructors to use detection tools: P40.
units.anchor: Become familiar with available tools that can help detect AI-generated text

units.why: "Discuss the potential consequences of misusing AICGTs, such as academic penalties or ethical issues" tells instructors to talk about consequences; P37 fits partly because no specific penalty is stated.
units.anchor: Discuss the potential consequences of misusing AICGTs, such as academic penalties or ethical issues

units.why: "Uploading student work to external AI detection tools may result in FERPA, privacy, and copyright violations" warns instructors against uploading student work to detectors: P50.
units.anchor: Uploading student work to external AI detection tools may result in FERPA, privacy, and copyright
